scenario.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Mandiant & MITRE — Azure VM CustomScriptExtension & IMDS Managed Identity Token Audit
scenario.overview: Picture a stately national art museum gallery with framed paintings on marble walls, velvet stanchion ropes, illuminated glass display pedestals, and thin security laser beams. Inside the hushed art museum hall, a thief studies how the velvet stanchions and glass pedestal sensors respond to routine curator maintenance checks. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the museum curator's station. During closing inspection, the museum curator checks the gallery motion-sensor log and spots a brief laser shadow that never matched any scheduled restoration. In this scenario (T1059, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Mandiant & MITRE, Azure VM CustomScriptExtension & IMDS Managed Identity Token Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: aRM Control-Plane, then guest Agent SYSTEM Child Process Execution, then local IMDS Managed Identity OAuth Token. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering ARM Control-Plane, then Guest Agent SYSTEM Child Process Execution, then Local IMDS Managed Identity OAuth Token, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: ARM Control-Plane Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write Invocation
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter)
stages.description: Inside the hushed art museum hall, a thief studies how the velvet stanchions and glass pedestal sensors respond to routine curator maintenance checks. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the velvet rope gallery entrance in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the museum curator go about their routine. Holding RBAC permissions on the subscription or resource group, the actor dispatches an ARM PUT request to Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write (or runCommand/action), recorded in AzureActivity logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with ArmOperation=MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/EXTENSIONS/WRITE, ExtensionType=Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension, TargetVirtualMachine=prod-app-vm01 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/EXTENSIONS/WRITE" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , AzureActivity | where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/EXTENSIONS/WR so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1059 during "ARM Control-Plane Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write Invocation" , Holding RBAC permissions on the subscription or resource group, the actor dispatches an ARM PUT request to Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write , or runCommand/action, recorded in AzureActivity logs while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact az vm extension list --resource-group prod-rg --vm-name prod-app-vm01 runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , az vm extension list --resource-group prod-rg --vm-name prod-app-vm01 against AWS CloudTrail so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1059 during "ARM Control-Plane Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write Invocation" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). stages.title: Stage 2: Guest Agent (WaAppAgent.exe / walinuxagent) SYSTEM Child Process Execution
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1078.004 - Cloud Accounts)
stages.description: Using a mirror-angle trick that satisfies the glass case laser beam, the thief lifts the cover and swaps a priceless artifact for a weight-matched replica. Here in Step 2 inside the art museum, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the laser-guarded glass display case without disturbing the permanent restoration wing. Inside the guest OS, the Azure VM Agent (WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe or walinuxagent) downloads the extension payload into C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension\ (or /var/lib/waagent/custom-script/download/) and executes it as SYSTEM/root (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with ParentAgent=C:\WindowsAzure\Packages\WaAppAgent.exe, PluginDirectory=C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension\1.10.12\Downloads\0\, ExecutionIntegrity=NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe", "enable.cmd") (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , DeviceProcessEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any , "WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe" so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1078.004 during "Guest Agent , WaAppAgent.exe / walinuxagent SYSTEM Child Process Execution" , Inside the guest OS, the Azure VM Agent , WindowsAzureGuestAgent while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ls -la /var/lib/waagent/custom-script/download/0/ runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ls -la /var/lib/waagent/custom-script/download/0/ via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1078.004 during "Guest Agent , WaAppAgent.exe / walinuxagent SYSTEM Child Process Execution" , Inside the guest OS, the Azure VM Agent , WindowsAzureGuestAgent while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted -File C:\Packages\Plugins\Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension\1.10.12\Downloads\0\diag_collect.ps1 / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Azure Resource Manager (ARM API)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) & Key Vault).

stages.title: Stage 3: Local IMDS (169.254.169.254) Managed Identity OAuth Token Acquisition & Key Vault Read
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.005 - Cloud Instance Metadata API)
stages.description: The glass pedestal seals back down without tripping the lobby bell, leaving visitors admiring a convincing decoy behind the velvet ropes. In this final step inside the art museum, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the museum curator's station until the gallery motion-sensor console catches the mismatch. Running inside the VM, the script queries http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://vault.azure.net with header Metadata: true to obtain the VM System-Assigned Managed Identity token and read Azure Key Vault secrets (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with MetadataEndpoint=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token, KeyVaultOperation=SecretGet , sql-conn-string, CallerIdentity=System-Assigned Managed Identity , prod-app-vm01 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs | where ServicePrincipalName == "prod-app-vm01" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs | where ServicePrincipalName == "prod-app-vm01" via System / Ru so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.005 during "Local IMDS , 169.254.169.254 Managed Identity OAuth Token Acquisition & Key Vault Read" , Running inside the VM, the script queries http://169 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact AzureDiagnostics | where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT" and OperationName == "SecretGet" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , AzureDiagnostics | where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT" and OperationName == "Secr so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.005 during "Local IMDS , 169.254.169.254 Managed Identity OAuth Token Acquisition & Key Vault Read" , Running inside the VM, the script queries http://169 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ GET https://prod-fin-kv.vault.azure.net/secrets/sql-conn-string?api-version=7.4 / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 Azure Resource Manager (ARM API)) to Node ④ (#4 Azure VM WaAppAgent / CustomScriptExtension), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Azure IMDS (169.254.169.254) & Key Vault).
